chapters.note: The recollection, named places and judicial commands retain their order. Ordinary address uses you/your; earlier notes preserve observations about singular and plural Greek forms.
Names, territories, measures and the inherited Seir readings remain. The commands concerning neighbouring peoples and the reported violence have not been harmonized or softened.
Moses’ prayer in 3:24 retains Thou/Thy/Thine. God’s reply and commands to human recipients use you/your. The geographical names, iron bed and stated dimensions remain.

The images of fire, the iron furnace, voice and likeness remain. Negatives and the question in 4:34 have clearer English. Earlier notes retain the source’s changes between singular and plural address.

The inherited commandment order is retained: adultery precedes murder in 5:17–18. Commands address people and use you/your; the quoted divine speaker is not the addressee. The source’s repeated covenant language remains.
The preface within 6:4, heart and soul in 6:6, immovable sign in 6:8 and mercy in 6:25 remain. Ordinary address uses you/your. Selected main-text inspection does not replace full independent review.
The named nations, commands, covenant and repeated warnings remain. The inherited spoil and wounded wording in 7:16 and 7:21 remains provisional. English changes do not make a new textual choice.
The wilderness, hunger, manna, garments, feet and land images remain. The bread-and-word sentence and negatives have clearer English order. “Mine copper” retains mine as a verb.
Moses’ prayer in 9:26–29 retains Thou/Thy/Thine/Thyself, including the inherited King of the gods address. Repeated strength and arm language remains. The two negatives in 9:23 are explicit.
The itinerary, Aaron’s death, levitical service and seventy souls remain. The inherited shift from plural Levites to singular his inheritance has not been silently levelled. Commands use you/your.

The long opening recollection and its supplied English connection remain. The enlarged-heart image in 11:16 is retained, with its earlier explanation available. Conditional negatives have clearer English.
The chosen place, offerings, blood and provision for the Levite remain. Ordinary address and negative clauses are revised; the distinctions among sacrifice, ordinary slaughter and eating remain.

All 19 source-numbered units remain, including the opening prohibition on adding or taking away. Conditional verbs use ordinary present-tense English. The agents and reported penalties remain explicit.
Animal and bird names, purification wording and the lamb in its mother’s milk remain as inherited provisional renderings. The tithes and provisions for the sojourner, orphan and widow remain.

Release, lending, service, gifts and firstborn provisions retain their distinctions. Attributive your and possessive yours are distinguished. The inherited yearly-wage wording in 15:18 remains provisional.
The festival order, boiling and roasting in 16:7, permitted needs in 16:8 and repeated feast names remain. Sentence order is clearer; the inherited phrases about just judgment remain.
Witnesses, judicial decisions, the ruler and the written second law remain. Conditional grammar is modernized without compressing repeated legal distinctions or royal restrictions.

Priestly portions, prohibited practices and the promised prophet retain their distinct terms. The inherited manifestations-related terminology elsewhere is not imported here. Negative syntax in 18:22 is clearer.

The distinction between unintentional killing and murder, refuge cities, witnesses and proportional penalties remains. Conditional verbs and the purpose of preventing innocent bloodshed have clearer grammar.
The account’s exemptions, offer of peace, siege and tree question remain. The reported violence is not euphemized. English changes do not settle the inherited dependent-household interpretation.
The prayer in 21:8 retains Thy/Thou. The heifer procedure, captive woman, inheritance, rebellious son and hanging provisions remain in their existing order, with their stated agents and penalties.

Lost property, roof parapet, mixtures, marriage and sexual-violence provisions retain their distinctions. Conditional verbs and negatives are clearer; no modern legal interpretation is substituted for the text.

All 26 source-numbered units remain, including the opening father’s-wife prohibition and the grain/vineyard order. Assembly, camp, escaped-slave, interest and vow provisions retain their inherited wording.
The divorce sequence, pledges, wages, individual liability and gleaning provisions remain. Conditional verbs use ordinary present-tense English. Mercy in 24:13 remains as inherited.
The limit on stripes, unmuzzled ox, levirate provisions, measures and Amalek command remain. Conditional grammar and negatives are revised; quantities, bodily language and penalties are preserved.

The confession shifts from speaking about God to addressing Him. Within 26:10 and 26:13, human instructions use you/your while the prayer retains Thou/Thy. The second tithe and inherited Syria wording remain.

The stones, Ebal/Gerizim assignments and every repeated response remain. The additional wife’s-sister clause in 27:23 is retained. Ordinary address and the negative in 27:26 follow the Bespoke convention.

All 69 units remain, including the covenant heading at 28:69. The blessing and curse wishes retain their grammatical force; famine, siege and bodily images are not softened. Until-clauses have clearer grammar.

All 28 source-numbered units remain. The inherited sinner/guiltless interpretation in 29:18 remains a priority for independent syntax review. The visible/hidden distinction and covenant wording remain.
The inherited healing of sins, cleansing of the heart and word in mouth, heart and hands remain. The life-and-death appeal retains its repetitions; conditional grammar is clearer.

Joshua’s commission, the seven-year reading, the song as witness and the law beside the ark remain. Imperatives have natural English word order; the inherited identification of the speaker in 31:23 remains.

The Song of Moses retains its imagery, angels of God in 32:8, the expanded 32:43, and repeated “See, see” in 32:39. Difficult wording, including 32:5, 32:24 and 32:36, remains provisional for independent review.

The blessing retains its changes of addressee. Divine address remains in 33:3, 33:7 and 33:9–10; the human-directed quotation in 33:9 uses you. Inherited manifestations, wrath, animal and tribal images remain provisional.

The inherited plural “they buried him”, Gai, cheeks and spirit of understanding remain after selected main-text inspection. Moses’ death and Joshua’s succession keep their distinct agents and wording.

scope: English editorial review; selected main-text checks. Full independent Greek, apparatus, reception and human read-aloud reviews remain pending.
